title: manifest-replication-lag-mixed-bin-apply-incident
summary: During a staged canary rollout of the quantized model bundle (v2.3-q8), we observed a subset of inference workers applying a mixture of old and new binary artifacts due to manifest replication lag. The mixed-apply caused tokenizer mappings and KV cache layout differences across machines which led to increased hallucination rate in the canary cohort and sporadic embedding dimension errors in downstream rerankers. We paused the rollout, rolled the canary back to the previous atomically-signed manifest, and implemented mitigations to prevent partial applies in future rollouts.
detection: Automated canary monitors flagged a 2.4x increase in hallucination-rate metric for the canary traffic at 2024-09-12T02:13:00Z. Concurrently, the canary healthcheck suite returned tokenization mismatch warnings from the synthetic prompt set and Sentry alerted to rare downstream ValueError exceptions in the reranker due to unexpected embedding shapes. Ops on-call observed a correlated p95 latency increase of ~180ms for canary nodes.
timeline: 2024-09-12T01:45:00Z - Release pipeline published manifest v2.3-q8 to manifest-store (publisher service).
2024-09-12T01:47:30Z - Orchestrator started canary rollout to zone-a (10% of traffic).
2024-09-12T02:11:05Z - Canary monitors begin to show elevated hallucination metric; SRE alerted automatically.
2024-09-12T02:13:00Z - On-call runs canary healthcheck; tokenization mismatch and embedding shape errors observed in logs.
2024-09-12T02:22:00Z - Investigation finds differing manifest checksums across zone-a and zone-b workers; some workers show old manifest while others show new, but both report "applied" state.
2024-09-12T02:30:00Z - Rollout paused via orchestrator kill-switch; traffic moved off canary nodes to stable fleet.
2024-09-12T03:05:00Z - Force-reverted canary group to prior signed manifest v2.2 and verified checksum consistency across zones.
2024-09-12T06:40:00Z - Post-incident cleanup: re-run artifact audit and snapshot verification; begin remediation tasks for manifest store and publisher service.
2024-09-20T09:00:00Z - Draft of this postmortem and runbook updates created.
impact: User-facing impact was limited to the canary cohort (10% traffic) but the canary is the upstream signal for promoting releases; observable impacts included degraded response quality (hallucinations/unexpected tokenization behavior) and intermittent downstream reranker errors causing 500s for a tiny fraction of requests. No production traffic on stable fleet was affected because the rollout was still in canary when paused.
mitigation: Immediate actions: 1) paused the rollout using the orchestrator kill-switch, 2) drained canary nodes and routed traffic back to v2.2, 3) forced manifest re-sync across all workers and validated checksums, 4) rolled back publisher changes that had introduced a manifest state field change. Longer-term mitigations implemented within 48 hours: gated manifest apply with a pre-apply checksum validation, enforce manifest-version pinning on worker boot, and add cross-zone manifest-consistency checks before allowing a rollout to proceed beyond canary.
root_cause: Race condition between the manifest publisher and worker bootstrap: the publisher uploaded a new manifest that exceeded a multipart threshold and for a short window returned inconsistent listing results from the manifest-store replication layer. Workers that read the manifest during the inconsistent window saw a manifest header that included the new version but fetched some binary shards from the previous version due to replication lag. The orchestrator assumed apply was atomic because workers reported 'applied' after receiving a mix of blobs — our apply path lacked end-to-end checksum validation and atomic rename semantics for the manifest directory. Contributing factors: (a) manifest-store replication is eventually consistent for multi-part uploads, (b) publisher omitted a final manifest-state marker on first write attempt due to a transient S3 error fallback path, and (c) the worker apply logic did not verify per-file checksums before marking 'applied'.
contributing_factors: No gating on manifest completeness, insufficient end-to-end integrity checks, lack of canary-level inter-node consistency validation, and an untested interaction between multipart upload behavior and manifest-store replication. The new quantization pipeline increased artifact size by ~12%, pushing the manifest upload into a different code path (multipart) that exercised an edge case.
postmortem_actions: INF-2024: Add atomic manifest publish protocol - replace open write with two-phase commit and final 'manifest-ready' marker (owner: platform-engineering, due: 2024-10-05).
INF-2025: Worker-side checksum verification - require per-shard SHA256 validation before marking manifest applied (owner: serving-runtime, due: 2024-09-30).
INF-2026: Pre-rollout cross-zone manifest parity check - orchestrator must verify identical checksums in 3 zones before traffic shift beyond canary (owner: release-engineering, due: 2024-10-03).
INF-2027: Extend canary healthchecks to include tokenization and embedding-shape tests in the synthetic suite (owner: applied-ml, due: 2024-09-25).
INF-2028: Add alerting for mixed-manifest-apply patterns based on inconsistent checksums reported by workers (owner: site-reliability-engineering, due: 2024-09-27).
INF-2029: Post-deploy validation job that re-reads manifest-store listing after 30s and compares object checksums; fail rollout if mismatch (owner: platform-engineering, due: 2024-10-10).
runbook_changes: Runbook: 'canary-manifest-apply-checklist' updated to include pre-rollout manifest parity verification (step 2), required per-shard checksum check (step 4), and a fast rollback playbook if tokenization-mismatch>=threshold in synthetic tests. Added explicit command snippets and a new 'manifest-consistency' CLI utility. On-call cheat-sheet added: how to force a full manifest re-sync, how to read the per-worker applied-checksum.log, and who to page for publisher rollbacks.
lessons_learned: Atomicity and integrity across artifact distribution are critical for model rollouts; small changes in artifact size or transport path can surface latent assumptions. Canary cohorts are doing their job — they caught a real cross-node consistency issue that would've had broader impact if promoted. This incident highlights the need for stronger end-to-end verification rather than relying on 'applied' flags from workers.
notes_to_oncall: If you see asymmetric checksums during rollout: 1) pause rollout immediately, 2) run manifest-consistency CLI against all affected zones, 3) drain canary nodes and fail traffic back to stable, 4) collect applied-checksum.log from 3 nodes (one per AZ) and upload to incident channel, 5) do NOT attempt to re-publish manifest until platform-engineering has validated the publish protocol. Use channel #sre-incidents and tag @platform-eng on call.
appendix_artifact_checks: Collected sample diffs: worker-01 applied: manifest-v2.3 header with tokenizer-v3 mapping, shard-12 from v2.2 binary; worker-03 applied: full v2.3 shards. Checksum mismatch table attached to Jira JIRA-5432 (see linked_artifacts).
